beefs.subject: The arts bill photo-op
beefs.a_says: He promised me the podium at his arts-funding announcement — my face, his bill. Then his office 'restructured the optics.' I found out from a press release.
beefs.b_says: The bill needed votes, not a movie star, and her last picture tested poorly with my district. That's not betrayal, my friend, that's polling.

beefs.subject: A donation that bounced
beefs.a_says: I wrote his campaign a check when I still believed in checks. Now he won't return my calls. Politicians remember donors, not friends.
beefs.b_says: The check bounced. Twice. I would love to forget it, but my treasurer laminated it.

beefs.subject: The missing earring
beefs.a_says: At last year's gala an emerald earring vanished from the powder room, and the staff were the only ones in and out. I never accused anyone. I merely mentioned it. Loudly.
beefs.b_says: She had me searched in front of the kitchen staff. The earring was in her own coat lining. She never apologized, because to her, we're furniture that talks.

beefs.subject: The wet canvas
beefs.a_says: I moved her canvas six inches to dust a shelf. Six inches. She reacted like I'd burned the Louvre.
beefs.b_says: She put her thumb through a wet study worth more than her yearly wages, then dusted around it. I painted her into the mural afterwards. As a lamp.

beefs.subject: The NDA after the breakup
beefs.a_says: When James ended it, this man slid an NDA across the table like a dessert menu. Three years of my life, reduced to a document with my name spelled wrong.
beefs.b_says: Mr. Braun instructed; I drafted. For the record, I spelled her stage name correctly — she signed her legal one. And she signed fast, for someone so heartbroken.

beefs.subject: The property assessment
beefs.a_says: His surveyors walked my hedgerow with clipboards like an invading army. Three acres, ten years of peaceful use, gone because this man bills by the hour.
beefs.b_says: He was mowing my client's land and calling it his. I sent one letter. He sent back a fruit basket with a threat in the card. I kept the card. Lawyers keep everything.

beefs.subject: The corrected lecture
beefs.a_says: I audited his criminology guest lecture and he got the chain-of-custody rules wrong, so I raised my hand. Facts don't care about tenure.
beefs.b_says: She interrupted me eleven times. I counted, because counting was the only thing keeping me from a crime of my own.

beefs.subject: The paper about her father
beefs.a_says: He published a paper on 'regional organized crime networks' with my father's name in a footnote. A footnote! My family is not your citation.
beefs.b_says: Her father's case is public record and academically significant. I offered to send her the full text. She offered to show me her nine iron.

beefs.subject: The expose that killed the deal
beefs.a_says: Her little finance piece ran the same week my last investor was deciding. He read it on a Tuesday and was gone by Friday. She didn't report my collapse, she catered it.
beefs.b_says: Every number in that piece was true, and he knows it, because he's the one who leaked half of them trying to get sympathy coverage. Wrong reporter.

beefs.subject: Barred from the docks
beefs.a_says: I asked one question about his manifests and suddenly there's a photo of me at the harbormaster's office with 'DO NOT ADMIT' under it. Innocent men don't laminate.
beefs.b_says: The docks are dangerous for civilians, especially ones who count other people's crates. I had her barred for her safety. Mostly her safety.

beefs.subject: The portrait she wouldn't pay for
beefs.a_says: She painted me last spring and made me look — her word — 'clinical.' I declined to purchase it. That is a consumer choice, not a scandal.
beefs.b_says: I painted what sat in front of me: a woman watching everyone in the room like patients she hadn't billed yet. She offered double to destroy it. I keep it in my studio, facing the door.

beefs.subject: The stonewalled records
beefs.a_says: He requested a deceased patient's records with a warrant that covered half of what he asked for. I gave him exactly the half. He's resented arithmetic ever since.
beefs.b_says: A man died under her care with a toxicology report that read like a shrug, and she buried the file in procedure. I don't forget shrugs.

beefs.subject: The suitor she didn't pick
beefs.a_says: I courted her first — two dinners and a regatta — and she chose the bigger house. I have a lake, madam. He has a pond with opinions.
beefs.b_says: Two dinners where he talked about drainage, and a boat race he lost. I didn't choose the bigger house. I declined the smaller man.

beefs.subject: The 3 a.m. drive
beefs.a_says: She wanted me to drive her friends home at three in the morning, off the books, off my shift. I said no. She tried to have me fired by breakfast.
beefs.b_says: I asked for one favor in eight months of her sitting in my driveway judging my guests. Staff who pick and choose their loyalty aren't loyal. Remember I said that.

beefs.subject: The charity golf disaster
beefs.a_says: She coached my celebrity foursome at that charity tournament and let us be humiliated on camera. A real professional protects her clients from the truth.
beefs.b_says: I gave her three lessons and one invoice. She paid for neither, then told the gala that golf 'isn't cinematic.' My sport paid for this dress, darling.

beefs.subject: The tabloid story
beefs.a_says: When he was broke — the first time — he sold a story about me to a tabloid. On-set behavior. Sourced 'close to the production.' He was close to the buffet.
beefs.b_says: I sold them three paragraphs of things she said in front of forty people. Public performance, public record. If she wanted privacy she should have whispered, once, ever.

beefs.subject: The missing shipment
beefs.a_says: A delivery for my spring gala never arrived — forty cases, prepaid, poof. He blamed the weather. Weather does not steal, darling. Suppliers do.
beefs.b_says: The shipment arrived. Her people signed for it. Where forty cases go after a woman like that signs is a question for her accountant, her confessor, or her flask.

beefs.subject: The foundation she declined
beefs.a_says: Her foundation asked me to manage its endowment. I reviewed the books and declined, in writing, twice. Some numbers you don't touch without gloves.
beefs.b_says: She turned down a charity, then told half the county it was 'a compliance decision.' Bankers guard money that helps no one and call it ethics.

beefs.subject: The robbery at her club
beefs.a_says: Her old club got robbed twice in a year and both times the safe was emptied between sets — her sets. I asked her about the timing. She sang me her answer. It didn't rhyme with innocent.
beefs.b_says: He questioned me for two hours like I'd cracked the safe with a high C. The club's owners robbed themselves for the insurance, and he knows it. He just liked the show.

beefs.subject: Mocked from the stage
beefs.a_says: She read my motivational post out loud at her show — 'the grind respects no storm, champ' — and the whole room laughed. That post helped people. Probably.
beefs.b_says: It was a good bit. He got two hundred new followers off it and sent me an invoice for 'brand usage.' An invoice! For a heckle!

beefs.subject: The plates she ran
beefs.a_says: The trainee ran my plates 'for practice.' Twice. Practice on someone who can't check the logs and see your name, kid.
beefs.b_says: Random selection, standard exercise — and for the record, her registration history has a two-year gap in it. I wasn't looking for anything. Then I found something.

beefs.subject: The document dump
beefs.a_says: On my ride-along we caught his aide feeding a shredder in a parking garage at midnight. The report got 'administratively resolved' in four days. I kept my copy.
beefs.b_says: An overzealous staffer disposed of duplicate constituent mail, and an overzealous cadet turned it into a spy novel. I resolved it like an adult: quietly.

beefs.subject: The book he never filmed
beefs.a_says: He optioned my family tell-all for a pittance, sat on it for six years, and let the rights expire the week my creditors called. My story funded nothing, including me.
beefs.b_says: I optioned it as a favor and read it as a punishment. Two hundred pages of a man blaming a house. There's no third act, Harry. There's barely a first.

beefs.subject: The tidied guest room
beefs.a_says: I stayed here last spring and the maid rearranged my papers — my papers — into neat little stacks. Financial papers. Then a reporter knew my numbers. Draw the line yourself.
beefs.b_says: I cleaned a room that looked burgled and made it look inhabited. If his 'numbers' were secret, perhaps don't leave them under a room-service tray with the syrup.

beefs.subject: The lobby commission
beefs.a_says: I commissioned a lobby piece and negotiated the price like I negotiate everything. She took it personally. Artists invoice in feelings.
beefs.b_says: She offered a third of my rate and called it 'exposure to serious capital.' I painted the lobby of the bank across the street instead. Bigger lobby.

beefs.subject: The cease-and-desist
beefs.a_says: I painted the Braun estate gates from a public road and this man sent me a cease-and-desist on letterhead thick enough to frame. So I framed it. It hangs next to the painting.
beefs.b_says: The gates feature a security configuration my client preferred unpublicized. Nothing personal. She retaliated by painting my office building. Badly, I'm told.

beefs.subject: The leaked 'before' photos
beefs.a_says: He used my 'before' photos in his marketing. My before photos, on a banner, at a health fair. I have a lake, and now four thousand strangers know I had a gut.
beefs.b_says: He signed the media release, champ. Page two, initialed. And that 'after' photo took us eight months — those results deserved an audience.

beefs.subject: 'Mostly reproductions'
beefs.a_says: At my own dinner table, this man swirled my brandy and announced my collection was 'mostly reproductions, and cheerful ones.' In front of my banker.
beefs.b_says: He asked my professional opinion in front of witnesses. The Vermeer is a poster. It was framed with the museum-shop barcode intact. What was I to do, lie in Latin?

beefs.subject: The blocked public course
beefs.a_says: I championed a public golf course for kids on the east side. He killed it in committee, then showed up at my tournament for photos. I made him putt. On camera. He missed.
beefs.b_says: The land had drainage issues and the funding had her name on it in letters I found presumptuous. And the green was doctored. Nobody misses by that much.

beefs.subject: The article about her father
beefs.a_says: I wrote one profile that mentioned her father's history — three paragraphs in a two-thousand-word piece, all documented. She's iced me at every event since.
beefs.b_says: Three paragraphs was the headline, the pull-quote, and the photo caption. My tournament win got one sentence. Journalists count words the way I count strokes: dishonestly.

beefs.subject: The service entrance
beefs.a_says: He pressured me for weeks to leave the service entrance unlocked for his 'late deliveries.' Off the ledger, he said, like the ledger was the crime.
beefs.b_says: I offered the young lady a standard consideration for flexible receiving hours. Every great house in this county has an arrangement. Hers is the only one that lectures.

beefs.subject: Her medical opinion of his product
beefs.a_says: I told a patient his brandy was, medically speaking, an aggressive solvent. Word traveled. He's been theatrical about it ever since.
beefs.b_says: This woman tells my customers my heritage label is poison. Poison! It's smoked plum and craftsmanship. If my brandy killed people, madam, I'd know exactly how.

beefs.subject: The soldier who walked
beefs.a_says: I spent two years building a case on a Syndicate enforcer, and this man got it thrown out on a filing timestamp. A timestamp. The next victim didn't get a timestamp.
beefs.b_says: The state broke procedure and I noticed. That's the entire job. He wants a justice system that only counts the rules he follows, and he calls that integrity.

beefs.subject: The background check
beefs.a_says: The week our engagement was announced, this man ran a background check on me. On a fiancee. I've been vetted like a hire, and now I know who filed it.
beefs.b_says: I ran it as a courtesy to a man I was working with. For the record, madam, it came back clean. Cleaner than most people's here. Curiously clean, an old cop might say.

beefs.subject: The trunk inspection
beefs.a_says: I caught him in the garage 'admiring' the cases in the trunk of Braun's town car with that little eyepiece of his. Admire from the curb, professor.
beefs.b_says: The cases bore auction-house stickers from a house that closed in disgrace. I examine provenance wherever it hides. She reacted like a woman guarding cargo, not a car.

beefs.subject: The one-star anecdote
beefs.a_says: She told a magazine her 'worst ride ever' story — the driver was 'silent, wore gloves, took the long way.' Everyone knew it was me. The long way avoided her ex's street. You're welcome.
beefs.b_says: It was a funny story and I never used her name. If she recognized herself in 'unsettling and glove-committed,' that's a her problem.

beefs.subject: The disinheritance coverage
beefs.a_says: When I was cut from the estate, her paper ran it with a photograph of me at my worst and a pun at my expense. 'Braun Out.' I've been a headline's punchline for nine years.
beefs.b_says: I didn't write the headline, I wrote the facts, and he confirmed every one of them on the record after his third gin. My notes say 'quote me, why not.' So I did.

beefs.subject: Dropped from the list
beefs.a_says: Darling, my events have standards, and the standard is solvency. The week he was disinherited, he tried to pay a gala pledge with a watch. A watch!
beefs.b_says: For twenty years I was at every table she set. One bad week and I vanished from her lists like a stain. That woman's loyalty is a coat-check ticket: keep the number or lose everything.

beefs.subject: The letters she stopped answering
beefs.a_says: I wrote to her all spring about historic medicinal plants for my monograph — dosages, preparations, the old pharmacopoeia. In June she simply stopped replying. Tonight I can't stop thinking about which letter was the last one.
beefs.b_says: A banker asking a physician for extraction methods on toxic botanicals is a correspondence one ends. I ended it. Politely. Ask her why she needed the dosages.

beefs.subject: The unpaid loan
beefs.a_says: When her club closed I lent her money — personally, no paperwork, against my every professional instinct. My instincts are undefeated. She still owes me.
beefs.b_says: She 'lent' me money and then priced the favor into every conversation since. I've paid that debt four times over in seating her next to interesting people. Bankers only count one currency.

beefs.subject: The skipped wedding sessions
beefs.a_says: She booked twelve bridal sessions and made four, then told the bridesmaids my program 'wasn't working.' Champ, the program can't run itself while you're at brunch.
beefs.b_says: He schedules sessions at six in the morning and calls anything less 'a mindset problem.' I'm getting married in six weeks. My mindset is fine. My patience is the thing that's toned.

beefs.subject: The park citation
beefs.a_says: She cited me for training clients in a public park. A public park! It's in the name! I framed the ticket and captioned it 'resistance training.'
beefs.b_says: Commercial activity in a public park requires a permit — it's forty dollars and a form. He'd rather be a martyr than fill out a form. The caption was funny though. I don't tell him that.
